data.title: Stocks have so far survived rising Treasury yields. But that may be about to change.
data.description:
By Michael Kramer

Strong earnings growth has cushioned the stock market from rising yields. But ever-rising bond rates may eventually take a toll.

S&P 500 earnings estimates have been rising, while the P/E ratio for the next 12 months has declined.

Treasury yields are rising, but stocks aren't falling.

That has investors trying to figure out how high the yield on the 10-year Treasury note needs to rise before the stock market finally cracks. But there probably isn't a magic number. What matters is whether rising rates begin to overwhelm the two forces that have protected stocks so far: earnings growth and low volatility in the bond market.

The earnings growth offset

The first point to note, which may be obvious, is that stocks aren't rising, either. The S&P 500 SPX is trading at about the same level it was on June 2, when the 10-year yield was at 4.45%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 index NDX is down about 5% from its June 2 closing high.

Things haven't been even worse because earnings estimates have been rising. As a result, the price-to-earnings ratio for the next 12 months has fallen to around 19.1, down from 21.3 on June 2. While the index has stalled, the P/E ratio has contracted by more than 9%. Earnings have grown 12.6% over that same period, from around $356 to $401. So higher earnings have offset the decline in the P/E ratio.

The opposite paths of the S&P 500's forward P/E (dark blue line) and its forward earnings per share.

It is easier to visualize the relationship between stocks and bonds using the S&P 500 earnings yield - the inverse of the P/E ratio - which has risen to 5.2% from around 4.7% since June 2. So while it may seem as if stock prices have been immune to the rise in Treasury rates, they haven't. In fact, stocks today are technically cheaper than they were prior to the recent move up in rates. It is just that earnings estimates have risen.

This is where things can get tricky for stocks. If at some point, the market begins to view higher rates as a drag on economic growth, potentially leading to lower earnings estimates, the S&P 500 could face a rather large decline. For example, if the S&P 500 traded at a 19.3 P/E ratio and earnings dropped back to $356, the index would trade around 6,870.

Alternatively, if the 10-year yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y continued to rise to, say, 5.25%, and the S&P 500 earnings yield rose in tandem to maintain the current spread of roughly 25 basis points, the earnings yield could climb to around 5.5%, corresponding to a P/E ratio of roughly 18.2. If earnings growth simply stopped at current levels, that would put the S&P 500 at around 7,280.

Right now, though, if earnings continue to grow, the index may remain relatively immune to a large drawdown, although it may not have much room for upside, either.

How the 10-year Treasury yield (red line) compares to the S&P 500 NTM earnings yield (blue line) from late 2023 to late 2026.

Bond-market volatility has remained low

Another factor is that bond-market volatility has remained low, despite rising rates. One reason stock markets reacted negatively in 2022 as Treasury rates rose was that earnings estimates fell and bond-market volatility rose sharply. To date, bond-market volatility has remained subdued, as measured by the Bank of America MOVE Index, which measures the bond market's implied volatility.

Historically, the MOVE Index and the S&P 500 have an inverse correlation, which means when bond-market implied volatility rises, stocks tend to fall. Right now, the 60-day rolling correlation is around -0.29, suggesting a relatively weak relationship. However, when MOVE rises quickly and reaches higher levels, that relationship tends to strengthen and turn more negative, increasing the pressure on stocks.

The ICE BofA MOVE Index and the S&P 500, along with their 60-day correlation, from 2021 to 2026.

However, despite the move higher in Treasury yields, we have not seen a meaningful change in volatility, allowing stocks, for the most part, to shrug off the rise in rates. If that changes and implied volatility begins to rise, it could quickly shift the equation for the equity market and lead to a more pronounced stock selloff.

Two factors to watch

Right now, stocks have been cushioned from rising bond yields because earnings growth has offset the P/E multiple contraction caused by higher rates, while bond-market volatility has remained subdued. If those conditions persist, the market may avoid a major drawdown, although further upside could become increasingly difficult.

The real risk, then, isn't that the 10-year Treasury yield reaches some predetermined level. It's that rising rates eventually weaken earnings expectations while also pushing bond-market volatility higher. If those two cushions disappear at the same time, the adjustment that has so far taken place almost entirely through valuation could quickly shift into stock prices.

Michael Kramer is the founder of Mott Capital Management and a long-only investor focused on macroeconomic themes. He analyzes long-term macro trends and short-term market risk using technical analysis, fundamentals and options-market positioning. See here for further disclosures.

-Michael Kramer

data.title: PRRS Responds to MPS Statements at the 2026 National Parking Association Conference & Expo
data.description:
PRRS Responds to MPS Statements at the 2026 National Parking Association Conference & Expo

PRRS Responds to MPS Statements at the 2026 National Parking Association Conference & Expo

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Sept. 15, 2026

LAS VEGAS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This Release is being circulated to address MPS's statements, including those made to customers of Parking Revenue Recovery Services, Inc. ("PRRS") and others attending the 2026 NPA Conference and Expo.

Status of asserted patent claims

In June 2025, MPS filed a complaint against PRRS asserting five counts of patent infringement. MPS's 2025 case is dormant, as the court ordered a stay pending the outcome of five pending Reexamination Proceedings before the United States Patent & Trademark Office ("USPTO").

As of today, four of MPS's asserted patents have received a Final Rejection issued by the USPTO. More specifically, MPS's patents have been reevaluated based on substantial new questions of patentability that the USPTO had not considered before, which include every asserted claim of U.S. Patent Nos. 11,257,302, 11,688,205, 12,142,085 and 12,249,187. In other words, the USPTO has determined that all asserted claims of these four patents are invalid – a claim PRRS has maintained throughout MPS's case.

Despite these Final Rejections, MPS filed a new complaint against PRRS in July 2026, raising a sixth patent, U.S. Patent No. 11,688,734. Due to the USPTO's determination of invalidity of MPS's prior patents, and the existence of substantial new questions of patentability, PRRS initiated a Reexamination Proceeding against the '734 Patent in August 2026.

In addition to these issues of invalidity, PRRS does not infringe upon any of MPS's patents, including U.S. Patent No. 11,688,734. MPS's prior statements to others in the parking industry have lead to an extensive countersuit by PRRS, which seeks: Judgment of Non-infringement; Judgment of Invalidity; Judgment of Unenforceability; Federal Unfair Competition; Intentional Interference with Contract; and Civil Conspiracy (among MPS and Premium Parking).1 If and when the 2025 case reopens, PRRS will vigorously pursue these remedies to address MPS's conduct, including MPS's continued enforcement of invalid patents.

Deadline Soon: Papa John’s International, Inc. (PZZA) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz About Securities Fraud Lawsuit

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz reminds investors of the upcoming November 2, 2026 deadline to participate as a lead plaintiff in the securities fraud class action lawsuit filed on behalf of investors who acquired Papa John’s International, Inc.(“Papa John’s” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PZZA) securities between August 7, 2025 and August 5, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”).

IF YOU ARE AN INVESTOR WHO LOST MONEY ON PAPA JOHN’S INTERNATIONAL, INC. (PZZA), CLICK HERE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SECURITIES FRAUD LAWSUIT.

What Happened?

On August 6, 2026, Papa Johns issued its second quarter 2026 financial results, reporting an 8.3% decline in North American comparable sales. The Company also reduced its fiscal 2026 outlook, expecting “global system-wide sales to decline between 2% and 4% compared to last year and adjusted EBITDA between $180 million to $190 million,” and suspended its quarterly dividend. During the related conference call, CEO Todd Allan Penegor stated that “it’s clear that our transformation is taking longer than expected” and “we must execute better and move faster.”

On this news, Papa Johns’ stock price fell $5.11 or 17.18%, to close at $24.64 per share on August 6, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What Is The Lawsuit About?

The complaint filed in this class action alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) Defendants created the false impression that they possessed reliable information pertaining to the effectiveness and ongoing impact of the Company’s strategic transformation as well as their resulting projected growth outlook for the North American region; (2) Defendants also minimized the risk of cautious consumer sentiment, competition woes, promotional seasonality, and more general macroeconomic fluctuation; (3) In truth, Papa Johns’ strategic transformation was taking considerably longer than the projections had suggested and the Company was simply ill equipped to “meet the consumer where they're at;” and (4) as a result, Defendants’ positive statements about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

If you purchased or otherwise acquired Papa John’s International, Inc. securities between August 7, 2025 and August 5, 2026, the deadline to seek appointment as the lead plaintiff in the securities fraud class action is November 2, 2026.

data.title: Investor Notice: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of the Baidu, Inc. Class Action Lawsuit
data.description:
Investor Notice: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of the Baidu, Inc. Class Action Lawsuit

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP informs investors that a class action was filed on behalf of persons and entities who purchased or otherwise acquired Baidu, Inc. (NASDAQ: BIDU) securities, including call options, between November 18, 2025 and August 17, 2026, inclusive (the Class Period). Baidu is a Chinese technology company which operates the most popular internet search engine in China.

The complaint alleges that Baidu, Inc. overstated the ability of its AI business to mitigate rapid declines in its legacy online marketing business;

Investors who suffered significant losses during the Class Period may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit and should contact Robbins LLP for information.

Why Was Baidu Sued?

Plaintiff alleges that online Marketing Services is Baidu’s core legacy business, which represented approximately 53.1% of total revenues for the third quarter of 2025. However, Online Marketing Services revenue for the third quarter of 2025 fell 17.6% compared to the third quarter of 2024. Despite this, Baidu assured investors that its new Core AI-powered Business growth had, and would continue to, meaningfully mitigate Baidu’s Online Marketing Services decline.

The complaint alleges that, during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose to investors:

(1) that the Company had overstated the ability of its AI business to mitigate rapid declines in its legacy online marketing business;
(2) that, as a result, the Company’s revenue was reasonably likely to decline; and
(3) that, as a result, defendants’ positive statements about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

Why Did BIDU Stock Drop?

The complaint alleges that on February 26, 2026, Baidu reported fourth quarter and full year 2025 financial results, revealing that total revenue fell more than 4% year over year for the fourth quarter to RMB32.74 billion (or $4.68 billion) and fell more than 3% year over year for the full year to RMB129.079 billion (or $18.458 billion). However, Baidu management assured investors its “AI-Powered Business” grew 48% year over year to RMB40 billion for fiscal year 2025, mitigating this transition. On this news, the price of Baidu American Depositary Shares (“ADS”) fell $7.50 per share or 5.65%, to close at $125.15 per share on February 26, 2026.

Then, on August 18, 2026, Baidu reported second quarter 2026 financial results, revealing that Baidu General Business revenue fell 4% year over year to RMB25.2 billion (or $3.71 billion), with Legacy Business revenue falling 23% year over year to RMB10.4 billion and total Online Marketing Services revenue falling 19% year over year to RMB13.1 billion. Critically, the Baidu Core AI-powered business fell 8% quarter over quarter to RMB12.5 billion (or $1.86 billion), its year-over-year growth having decelerated from 49% in the first quarter of 2026 to 25%, and its largest component, AI Cloud Infra, having fallen 17% quarter over quarter from RMB8.8 billion to RMB7.3 billion. On this news, the price of Baidu ADS fell $13.25 per share, or 12.73%, to close at $90.87 on August 18, 2026.

Who May Be Eligible to Participate in the Baidu Class Action?

The lawsuit seeks to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Baidu, Inc. securities between November 18, 2025 and August 17, 2026. Investors who suffered losses during that period may have legal rights under the federal securities laws.

What Is a Lead Plaintiff?

The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Serving as lead plaintiff is not required to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members if the case proceeds and later resolves successfully.

Stockholders who wish to lead the class action should contact Robbins LLP for information.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Baidu, Inc. securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

About Robbins LLP

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $1 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history.

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against Baidu, Inc. settles or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

data.title: Archer Roose Wines Named Impact Hot Prospect Brand Award Winner for Second Consecutive Year
data.description:
Archer Roose Wines Named Impact Hot Prospect Brand Award Winner for Second Consecutive Year

Recognition underscores Archer Roose Wines’ continued momentum and leadership in the wine category

Archer Roose Wines, the premium canned wine company founded by Marian Leitner-Waldman and co-owned by Elizabeth Banks, has been named a 2025 Hot Prospect Brand Award winner for the imported wine category by M. Shanken Communications’ Impact Databank. This is the second consecutive award for the brand, which requires depletions over 50,000 and double-digit depletions’ growth for three consecutive years. Archer Roose Wines grew 35% from 2024 to 2025 amidst continued declines for the broader wine category.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260915354980/en/

Founder and CEO, Marian Leitner-Waldman, and Co-Owner and Chief Creative Officer, Elizabeth Banks

The recognition marks an important milestone for Archer Roose Wines as the brand continues to outperform the wine category and lead within premium canned wine, building the category around a simple consumer need: a great glass of wine without the commitment of opening a full bottle.

“This recognition is meaningful because it reflects the strength of the business we’ve built,” said Marian Leitner-Waldman, Founder and CEO of Archer Roose Wines. “Archer Roose Wines was created to make quality wine more accessible, more flexible and more relevant to the way people want to enjoy wine today. Being named a Hot Prospect Brand Award winner once again reinforces that RTDs are evolving beyond spirits, and that premium canned wine has a real role to play in how today’s consumers discover and enjoy wine.”

The Hot Prospect Brand Awards recognize emerging beverage alcohol brands demonstrating strong sales and marketing achievement. For Archer Roose Wines, the award acknowledges continued momentum in the independent on-premise, where it sources ~80% of its volume, as well as within the retail and travel channels. Archer Roose Wines is unlocking growth by tapping into accounts previously underserved by the wine industry and providing an alternative to beers or hard seltzers.

Archer Roose Wines is known for its globally sourced wines, perfectly portioned 250mL cans and commitment to making premium wine easier to enjoy across more occasions, from restaurants and bars to travel to casual gatherings and everyday moments.

About Archer Roose Wines

Archer Roose Wines is the award-winning, globally sourced wine by the glass that leads with transparency and quality. Founded in 2015 by Marian Leitner-Waldman and co-owned by Chief Creative Officer Elizabeth Banks, the proudly women-led brand sources its portfolio from seven of the world's most renowned winemaking regions across five countries: Italy, France, Chile, Argentina, and Australia. Made in a low-intervention winemaking style with no added sugar, sustainably grown grapes, and 100% recyclable aluminum cans, Archer Roose Wines is built for the way modern consumers actually drink and allows for a great glass of wine without having to open a full bottle. The brand's portfolio is poured at premium hospitality partners including Cinemark and Regal Cinemas, Dave & Busters, Five Iron Golf and bars & restaurants nationwide and is stocked at retailers including Sprouts, BevMo!, Gopuff, Spec’s and Total Wine & More. You can also enjoy Archer Roose Wines on JetBlue, Princess Cruises and Breeze Airways. Learn more at www.archerroose.com.

data.title: "50X50: SCIENCE ACROSS AMERICA" GOES LIVE TODAY, UNITING THE BEST YOUTUBE CREATORS IN THE FIRST-EVER STATE-BY-STATE MEDIA INITIATIVE
data.description:
"50X50: SCIENCE ACROSS AMERICA" GOES LIVE TODAY, UNITING THE BEST YOUTUBE CREATORS IN THE FIRST-EVER STATE-BY-STATE MEDIA INITIATIVE

"50X50: SCIENCE ACROSS AMERICA" GOES LIVE TODAY, UNITING THE BEST YOUTUBE CREATORS IN THE FIRST-EVER STATE-BY-STATE MEDIA INITIATIVE

PR Newswire

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026

Launch day unites a creator roster with a combined YouTube reach of more than 90 million subscribers, spotlighting one homegrown creator and scientist in every state, with new videos rolling out region by region every week through mid-November

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 50x50: Science Across America, the first-ever nationwide media initiative to spotlight a YouTube creator in every U.S. state, officially launches today. The project unites a roster of creators paired with local scientists, whose channels command a combined total of more than 90 million YouTube subscribers — the biggest coordinated gathering of independent science voices ever assembled for a single campaign.

Created by The Independent Media Initiative, 50x50 includes, among others: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day (11.9M subscribers), Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown (8.6M), Adam Savage of Adam Savage's Tested (7.2M), Lily Hevesh of Hevesh5 (4.62M); Henry Reich of Minute Physics (5.94M), Emily Graslie of The Brain Scoop (606K); and Joe Hanson of Be Smart (5.8M). Other important voices included are: Laura Wilson of Laura Farms (875K); Jeremiah Burton of Big Time (1.95M); Anne Briggs of Anne of All Trades (732K); Xyla Foxlin (585K); and Tim Dodd of Everyday Astronaut (2M).

Beginning today and continuing region by region through November 2026, 50x50 will publish new state-by-state videos on a rolling ten-week schedule, moving from the Southwest through the South, Southeast, East, Northeast, Great Lakes, Midwest, Plains, Mountain, and West regions. Each installment pairs a homegrown creator whose video embodies that state's contribution to American science with a local scientist working in the community.

"50x50 is the world's biggest science media project ever done, and one of the biggest projects done on YouTube. We're introducing audiences to 50 scientists living and working in their own backyards, one state at a time." IMI President and co-founder Stuart Sevier said. "These creators represent the best of the internet, and we're proud to partner with them to create a true panorama of American science today."

50×50: Science Across America is presented by the Independent Media Initiative, in collaboration with Emmy award-winning HHMI Tangled Bank Studios, the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, the Winn Family Foundation, and the Shanahan Family Foundation, with additional support from the Allen Institute and The Brinson Foundation.

The initiative arrives at a moment when independent creators increasingly outpace traditional broadcast and cable outlets in reach among younger audiences. IMI describes 50x50 as both a media project and a national narrative: it's a large-scale portrait of how thoroughly science media has migrated to creator-led platforms, state by state, creator by creator.

Full creator biographies, the complete regional publication schedule, and participant and producer interview availability are available to press on request.

  Gias Foods recalled two lots of a fettuccine product sold under Walmart's Bettergoods brand due the risk of listeria. 



  The New York company recalled Authentic Italian Lemon Alfredo Fettuccine with UPC number 194346442706 and lot numbers L6079C or L6080C.
